content:
I worked a bit on making loogle (the CLI tool, and also the web interface) a bit easier to use locally. It’s still not quite as convenient as I want it to be, but should be simpler now – including more convenient managment of the precomputed index.

See <https://github.com/nomeata/loogle#running-locally> for details.

If you try it, let me know how it goes!

Now also has a --max-results options (@Michael Stoll)

Tried it and it works, thank you! (tried the CLI, haven't tried running the web interface yet)
Creating the Mathlib index took two and half minutes, though further queries take 10s-30s which is much slower than the actual Loogle.
Assuming most of the query time is to load the index from disk, hopefully running a local server will fix the performance.

That was quick!

You can use loogle --interactive to keep the CLI running and pass multiple queries per stdin, that should at least allow you to check if that hypothesis is true.

Can you clarify how much of the documentation (the README file) you plan to be written by you vs verbatim text generated by an LLM? perhaps this scale is useful, with "coded" repalced with "written" in describing your documentation writing plans: https://www.visidata.org/blog/2026/ai/#self-assessed-ai-level-for-contributions

I see today there are 5 commits to the README file with git commit title "README: ..." and commit message "Co-Authored-By: Claude ...".

It is difficult to quickly judge whether the README is you documenting your thoughts and understanding of this tool vs the output of an LLM.
Pro-tip: prefix the loogle command with rlwrap (requires non-Windows, and needs to be installed first), then you can use the arrow keys, and also the up arrow to edit a previous query
These commits were all done by my telling Claude what to put into the README
@Snir Broshi does the webserver work as well for you? (pull before trying, I made some more tweaks)
I think I broke some of the more interesting queries on the website. I won't be able to look into it for a few hours, though - sorry

Joachim Breitner said:

Snir Broshi does the webserver work as well for you?

Yes!
Seems to be working again, let me know of other issuea

Haven't heard much here. Have people started to use loogle this way, or still too tedious (or just not needed)?
@Oliver Dressler , did we talk about lean-lsp-mcp offering loogle locally by default? Do the changes above help in that way?
I have more important things to do, so this has moved down my todo list for the time being. But I may come back to what motivated my question at some later point.

Joachim Breitner said:

Haven't heard much here. Have people started to use loogle this way, or still too tedious (or just not needed)?

For me at least it was relatively easy to set up and quite useful :)
I have been using local Loogle for some time too, but it was also before the instructions revamp anyway. Still helpful though!

Joachim Breitner said:

or still too tedious

For me it is a bit of an annoyance to keep it up to date with the toolchain of every project I am working on, so I end up not using it locally. If I understand correctly, the MCP thing does this automatically but it's for agents, not for us humans. Couldn't there be some (VSCode?) action (or even a script) that sets this up for us humans, preferrably with the option of displaying the webserver?
Something like that might would be the next level, yes. To me that falls under a more general concept of “lake tool dependencies”.
